diurnal.structure: diurnal.<season> is a 24-value array (index = hour of day, 0 = 00:00-01:00 local standard time) of unitless multipliers with an exact discrete mean of 1.0. Multiply by a mean wind speed (or mean wind power) to get an hourly shape.
diurnal.methodology: Stylized single-cosine model, value(h) = 1 + amplitude*cos(2*pi*(h-16)/24), peaking at hour 16 (4pm) and troughing at hour 4 (4am), per meteorological season (winter=Dec-Feb amplitude 0.20, spring=Mar-May amplitude 0.38, summer=Jun-Aug amplitude 0.42, fall=Sep-Nov amplitude 0.30). This is a hand-authored model calibrated to match the qualitative diurnal pattern documented for California's Central Valley (afternoon/early-evening wind maximum, pre-dawn minimum, amplitude strongest in summer when the land-sea thermal contrast driving the "Delta Breeze" is largest), not a digitized instrument time series for the Lodi site specifically (no public hourly wind-speed climatology for Lodi was found).

sources.title: Diurnal Evolution of Three-Dimensional Wind and Temperature Structure in California's Central Valley
sources.note: Zhong et al., J. Applied Meteorology & Climatology 43(11), 2004. Documents a pronounced low-level diurnal wind oscillation in the Central Valley with a late-afternoon/early-evening speed maximum.

sources.title: Call me the (Delta) Breeze - our cooling Summer wind
sources.note: Describes the Delta Breeze: a thermally-driven afternoon/evening wind pulled into the Central Valley through the Sacramento-San Joaquin Delta, strongest in summer.

seasonal.structure: seasonal is a 12-value array (index 0 = January) of unitless monthly multipliers with an exact discrete mean of 1.0.
seasonal.methodology: Stylized single-cosine model, value(m) = 1 + amplitude*cos(2*pi*(m-7)/12) with amplitude 0.35, peaking in July and troughing in January. Calibrated to match the documented Delta Breeze / Altamont Pass windy season (elevated output May-October, per the Altamont Pass wind farm generation record), not a digitized wind-speed time series for Lodi specifically.

sources.title: Altamont Pass wind farm (Wikipedia)
sources.note: Notes the Altamont Pass (Central Valley/Delta wind resource area, same regional wind regime as Lodi) produces most of its electricity during the windy season, May through October.

powerCurves.structure: presets[].curve is an array of {ms, kw} points from the cited certification/manufacturer data, in ascending wind speed order. Values below the turbine's cut-in wind speed that were reported as small negative numbers (parasitic/controller power draw) in the source data have been clamped to 0 kW. Linear interpolation between points is expected at calculation time; do not extrapolate past the last point (treat wind speeds at or above the last curve point as flat-lined at that point's kw, since both source turbines exhibit power roll-off from blade pitch/stall regulation near cut-out that these tables do not fully capture). presets[].cutOutMS is optional: if a preset defines it, calculation should treat it as a hard shutdown above which output is 0 kW instead of flat-lining. Neither shipped preset defines one -- see each preset's notes.

presets.label: Bergey Excel 6
presets.notes: AWEA-rated power is 5.5 kW @ 11 m/s per SWCC certification; peak measured output ~6.6-6.7 kW near 16 m/s (model name "Excel 6" refers to the nameplate/marketing class, not the AWEA-rated figure). Bergey's own tower-requirements document (bundled in the SWCC report) specifies a 60 ft (18 m) minimum tower with 80 ft (24 m) or higher recommended; hubHeightDefaultM uses the manufacturer-recommended value. No cutOutMS: Bergey's published spec sheets give no operational shutdown wind speed for this model -- overspeed/furling protection is designed to hold the machine online up to its design wind speed (134 mph / ~60 m/s), well outside this curve's range -- so this preset intentionally has no cutOutMS and relies on the flat-line-above-last-point behavior.

sources.title: SWCC Summary Report - Bergey Excel 6 (Certification SWCC-10-11)
sources.note: Solar Rating & Certification Corporation (SRCC) / Small Wind Certification Council report per AWEA Standard 9.1-2009, including the tabulated power curve at sea-level air density (1.225 kg/m3) and AEP table.

sources.title: BERGEY EXCEL 6 Performance spec sheet
sources.note: Manufacturer performance sheet; lists cut-in and rated wind speed but no cut-out/shutdown wind speed.

presets.label: Southwest Windpower Skystream 3.7 (1.8 kW)
presets.notes: Manufacturer rated capacity is 1.8 kW rated / 2.4 kW peak; cut-in wind speed 3.5 m/s, rated wind speed 9.4 m/s, survival wind speed 63 m/s per manufacturer spec sheet. Skystream towers range 10.2 m (33 ft, used here as default) to 33.5 m (110 ft); taller towers increase energy yield. No cutOutMS: per the owner's manual, Skystream enters a self-limiting reduced-power mode above ~11 m/s (already reflected in the curve's flattening top end) and only fully shuts down above 29 m/s (65 mph) as a temporary storm response, restarting after about an hour. That is not a sustained-mean-wind-speed shutdown, so it does not map onto a static cutOutMS in an annual model; this preset relies on the flat-line-above-last-point behavior instead.

sources.title: Skystream 3.7 Technical Specifications (Southwest Windpower spec sheet DOC# 0370 REV D 4-07)
sources.note: Manufacturer spec sheet: rated capacity, cut-in/rated/survival wind speeds, rotor diameter, tower height range.

sources.title: NREL/turbine-models power curve archive - Skystream3.7_2.1kW_3.7.csv
sources.note: Tabulated wind-speed-vs-power-output curve (with Cp) used as the numeric curve source. The "2.1kW" in the archive filename reflects the field-tested peak bin, above the 1.8 kW nameplate rating.

sources.title: Skystream 3.7 Owner's Manual
sources.note: Describes storm-response behavior: enters reduced power mode above ~25 mph (11 m/s), and at 65 mph (29 m/s) shuts down for about one hour before resuming, rather than a permanent cut-out.
